walkthroughs.body_html:
Islam: Practices — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Islam: Practices brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Islam: Practices.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many times daily must Muslims pray?

options: The Shahada is the requirement to pray five times a day.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
The Islamic declaration of faith: 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah' — affirming monotheism and Muhammad's prophethood.
The Shahada is the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
The Shahada is the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hajj”?
options: Fasting from dawn to sunset throughout ninth month; no food, drink, smoking, sex; broken at iftar.
Pilgrimage to Mecca in Dhul-Hijjah; obligatory once if able; 2 million pilgrims annually circumambulate Kaaba.
Annual charity of 2.5% of accumulated wealth above nisab threshold; purifies remaining wealth; one of Five Pillars.
Sunni: Shahadah (declaration), Salah (prayer), Zakah (charity), Sawm (fasting), Hajj (pilgrimage).
